content.title: Final Four 2026: Lauren Betts, UCLA shut down Texas in 'ugly' game to reach national championship
content.text: The second game of the night in Friday’s women’s Final Four was the exact opposite of an offensive shootout. In fact, it was admittedly ugly at times.But Lauren Betts and the Bruins got the job done. For them, that’s all that matters.AdvertisementUCLA absolutely shut down Texas and Longhorns star Madison Booker offensively on Friday to pick up a 51-44 win in their national semifinal game at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. That sent the Bruins to the NCAA national championship game for the first time in program history.UCLA will take on South Carolina in the title game on Sunday afternoon (3:30 ET, ABC). The Gamecocks pulled away from No. 1 overall seed UConn in their Final Four game earlier on Friday, and head coach Geno Auriemma had to actually be separated from South Carolina coach Dawn Staley after a heated incident in the final moments. It marks the fourth time in the past five seasons that the Gamecocks have been to the championship game.UCLA shuts down Madison Booker, TexasUCLA held on to a three-point lead at the break after what was a very low-scoring first half. The Bruins opened the game on a 14-6 burst in the first quarter, while holding the Longhorns to just three made field goals in the opening period. Texas was held scoreless for more than four minutes during that stretch, too.AdvertisementBut Texas rallied back and held UCLA to just six points in the second quarter to get within a possession. Betts played a massive part in the Bruins’ defensive stand, holding Texas to 1-of-8 from the field when she was contesting their shots, and Booker went 0-of-5 against her. It was the lowest-scoring half by each team all season.Booker’s rough shooting night continued into the second half. She actually missed a career-high 17 field goals in a row before she finally made one as Betts and UCLA extended their lead. The two collided early in the third quarter, however, and Betts’ head slammed back onto the court hard. Betts was down for a few moments, but got up on her own and remained in the game as normal.But it was Justice Carlton who kept the Longhorns in it. She scored seven straight points for Texas to get them back within a possession. But even UCLA coach Cori Close knew how bad of a contest it had been up until that point.“I feel bad for the fans,” she said on ESPN. “31-28? I mean, it’s an ugly basketball game.”Whether it was Close’s words or not, the Bruins finally separated from Texas out of the final break. They started the fourth quarter on a 7-0 burst over a 90-second span, which included a 3-pointer from Kiki Rice and a Gabriela Jaquez fastbreak layup, to take a double digit lead once again.AdvertisementThe Longhorns did make one final push, but it came too late. After a 7-0 run that cut the score to a single possession inside the final minute, Betts stuffed Booker at the rim to seal their seven-point win and set up their matchup with the Gamecocks. The 95 combined points made it the third-lowest scoring Final Four game in history.“I think it was more rugby than it was basketball,” Close said on ESPN after the game. “I wanted to apologize to all the fans that we couldn’t give them a cleaner game, with 23 turnovers.”Kyla Oldacre was the only Texas player to hit double figures with her 11 points and seven rebounds off the bench. Booker finished with just six points while shooting 3-of-23 from the field.Betts led UCLA with 16 points and 11 rebounds after she went 7-of-10 from the field in the win. Rice added 11 points, and both Gianna Kneepkens and Jaquez finished with 10 points each. UCLA went just 4-of-13 from behind the arc and committed 23 turnovers.AdvertisementWhile it certainly wasn’t the best basketball, Close and the Bruins are moving on and now just a win away from the program’s first NCAA national championship.Live coverage is over27 updatesFri, April 3, 2026 at 8:35 PM CDTFri, April 3, 2026 at 10:54 PM CDTUCLA is headed to its first NCAA championship!
